clue.text: Aims to get it back within turns

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside the word for turns

parts.note: moves are turns in a game such as chess

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word it backwards

explanation.surface: Someone sets out their goals while going round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Motives are the purposes or reasons behind actions, so they are a person's aims.

clue.text: Setter's having faithful dog cooped up to make 18

definitions.note: 18 is small change, so to make a small change is a verb phrase meaning alter slightly

indicators.note: cooped as in cooped up: one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: the setter's is my, the crossword compiler speaking

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the dog's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Fido is the stock dog's name, from Latin for I trust

explanation.surface: The compiler keeps a loyal hound penned in to make some minor adjustment.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'cooped up' does two things: the dog's name is shut in and also reads upwards. The definition leans on 18, small change: to make a small change.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify something is to alter it slightly, making a minor adjustment to it.

clue.text: Maker of 5 across's 18

definitions.meaning: a craftsman who turns hides into leather
small change: an old British sixpenny coin

explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was British slang for the pre-decimal sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: One who cures hides makes leather; a tanner was also slang for the old sixpence, a small coin.

clue.text: Elevating island on condition that one clergyman can be confirmed

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevating lifts the whole run so it reads upwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
if means on condition that
one is the Roman numeral I
Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar's promotion on some island is conditional on his being vetted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevating' turns the whole run ELBA IF I REV upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something verifiable can be checked and shown to be true, so it can be confirmed.

clue.text: As judge's robes when changing ends

definitions.note: the idiom sober as a judge: read as what a judge is

indicators.note: the word robes has its first and last letters swapped round

explanation.surface: A judge's gown is described as it gets turned about.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the R and S at the ends of ROBES gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fixed simile is sober as a judge, so the word completes the comparison.

clue.text: Cordovan article with small jet frame

indicators.note: frame says one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a Learjet is a small business jet
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A Spanish-styled item is set inside the frame of a little aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordovan is a fine leather originally from Córdoba in Spain, so it is an example of leather.

clue.text: Alternatively, not very new or newish old language

definitions.text: Alternatively, not very new or newish old language

parts.words: Alternatively, not very new or newish old language
parts.note: an old tongue whose descriptor can mean either not very recent or fairly recent: the later form of the Romans' tongue

explanation.definitionFit: Late Latin is the form of the Roman language used in late antiquity, an old language whose first word means recent.

clue.text: Greeting from a boat?

parts.note: a hoy is a small coasting vessel

explanation.surface: A sailor calls out a hello from a passing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailor's call hailing another vessel is a nautical greeting.

clue.text: Stop on way to Brighton's pads

definitions.meaning: a village with a station on the London to Brighton railway line in Sussex

explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a seaside town on England's south coast; Hassocks is a stop on the railway there.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassocks is a Sussex village on the Brighton line; hassocks are also padded kneeling cushions.

clue.text: Salesman with a dark side of Chinese philosophy that's good for making good

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
yin is the dark, passive principle of yin and yang

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman with a shady streak finds Eastern thought useful for making amends.
explanation.definitionFit: Making good on a debt or wrong means repaying it.

clue.text: Giving one run's close on getting opener out

indicators.note: getting here means taking a letter in

parts.note: a door is what you open to get in

indicators.note: close means the end letter of run

explanation.surface: A batsman's generous innings ends when the opening player is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket words in the surface mislead: 'close' takes the N at the end of run, which goes into DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is someone who gives, so the phrase describing one who gives fits.

clue.text: Toast is behind drink

parts.note: the behind is the bottom, the backside
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Raising a glass is followed by more drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottoms up is a cheerful toast said before draining a glass.

clue.text: Mass uproar when gold's in uncontrollable descent

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: free fall is falling without restraint
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Panic breaks out when the price of gold plummets.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a disorderly brawl or uproar in which everyone joins.

clue.text: 1817's issue?

parts.note: read the numbers as two entries: the offspring of the tree-climbing marsupial, and an old threepenny coin, a piece of small change

explanation.definitionFit: A joey is a baby kangaroo, and a joey was also slang for a small silver coin, the threepenny bit.

clue.text: Officer's bad idea to run off in secret

indicators.note: bad tells us the word idea is rearranged

parts.note: to decamp is to leave suddenly and secretly

explanation.surface: A soldier's foolish plan is to desert quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is a military officer who acts as assistant to a senior commander.

clue.text: Very frightened by a direction to pile on points

parts.note: west is a compass direction
a rick is a stack or pile of hay
E and N are compass points

explanation.surface: Someone is scared by an order to heap up points.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestricken means filled with awe or dread, so greatly frightened.

clue.text: Background's disturbed in the metropolis

indicators.note: disturbed tells us the words in the are rearranged

parts.note: a metropolis is a big city

explanation.surface: Someone's past is unsettled in the big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnicity is one's cultural or racial origin, i.e. a person's background.

clue.text: When special force gets wrong killer

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he left
the SAS is the British Special Air Service
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: The special forces go astray when deployed.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, especially of a prominent person, so a killer.

clue.text: Organ developed in treeclimbing animal

indicators.note: developed says the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: the oak is a common tree

explanation.surface: An organ evolves inside a marsupial that lives up in the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree kangaroo is a real marsupial. 'developed' rearranges ORGAN with OAK, the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Kangaroos are leaping marsupials, and some kinds climb trees, so the answer is an example of a climbing animal.

clue.text: Something petty officer once announced at end of the line?

definitions.text: Something petty officer once announced at end of the line?

parts.words: Something petty officer once announced at end of the line?
parts.note: petty suggests minor coins; a railway guard once called out to passengers at the terminus that they must switch trains, and a petty one makes it a little call

explanation.definitionFit: Small change is loose coins of low value, something petty; it also echoes the guard's terminus cry of all change.

clue.text: Arctic cap doesn't have a right to regulate

indicators.note: doesn't have says some letters are removed

parts.note: the polar ice is the ice cap of the Arctic

explanation.surface: The northern ice sheet lacks any power of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't have' removes A and R from POLAR ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To police an activity is to control and regulate it.

clue.text: Animals having a set in 18

indicators.note: set in says a letter is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: 18 is small change, read as the word small changed, a rearrangement of small

explanation.surface: Creatures are put in for small change.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 18 as an instruction: SMALL rearranged gives LLAMS, then A goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American camelids, examples of animals.

clue.text: Vessel that carried naught to speak of

definitions.text: Vessel that carried naught to speak of

parts.words: Vessel that carried naught to speak of
parts.note: a ship whose crew of heroes had a name ending in a sound like naught, the Greek word for sailor

explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was Jason's ship, carrying the Argonauts, whose name ends in a syllable said like naught.

clue.text: Nothing reflected spot on lacy item without end product of flax

indicators.note: reflected tells us the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing
to spot is to see

indicators.note: without end tells us the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a doily is a lacy mat

explanation.surface: A lace mat shows its reflection without any mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns NIL into LIN; 'without end' drops the Y of DOILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed oil is pressed from the seeds of flax, so it is a product of that plant.

clue.text: Tree rising with power from grounds of university

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising says read upwards
from says something is taken out of the other word

parts.note: a campus is the grounds of a university

explanation.surface: A tree is growing on the college grounds with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking P 'from' CAMPUS leaves CAMUS, which 'rising' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree whose berries yield a spice.

clue.text: Open in Berlin and Oldenburg, initially

parts.note: und is German for and, as spoken in Berlin

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of Oldenburg

explanation.surface: Something is opened in two German cities.
explanation.walkthrough: Oldenburg is a German city; only its first letter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a parcel or button is to open it.

clue.text: Celestine's component symbolised by little Señor

definitions.meaning: celestine is a mineral, a sulphate of a metallic element
Sr, the abbreviation for Señor, is also this element's chemical symbol

explanation.definitionFit: Celestine is strontium sulphate, and Sr is both the element's symbol and the short form of Señor.

clue.text: Saw first team's second reversal

parts.note: A is first, as in A1 or grade A
an XI is a cricket or football team of eleven

indicators.note: reversal says the word for second is read backwards

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A saw cuts first while the team's number two flips.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, a synonym of an axiom.

clue.text: New coinage that's not 18

parts.note: coinage suggests money, but this is the minting of fresh words, not loose coins

explanation.definitionFit: Neology is the coining of new words, or a newly coined word.

parts.note: read as two entries: the law enforcers of 19 and the coins of 18

explanation.definitionFit: Coppers is slang both for police officers and for low-value copper coins.
